statements.quote: If Big Tech wants to build a massive data center and use massive amounts of electricity, they should pay for the power and infrastructure they need, not hardworking families and small businesses.
statements.context: He voted to advance H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, meant to keep consumers from paying for rising utility costs caused by AI data centers.
statements.reason: About electricity costs of AI data centers, which is outside catastrophic risk, so D.

statements.quote: but unfortunately there's a lot of unknowns, and I'm worried about our kids.
statements.context: In a story on AI power and safety, he praised AI as a technology that will develop cures, then voiced worry about children and pushed his bill to repeal Section 230 so AI and tech companies can be held responsible.
statements.reason: The worry named is harm to children, which is outside catastrophic risk, so D.

statements.quote: Now we’re learning the shooter may have interacted with ChatGPT before carrying this out.
statements.context: He called for accountability for Big Tech and repeal of Section 230 after a lawsuit linked ChatGPT to the April 2025 Florida State University shooting.
statements.reason: About a chatbot's possible role in one shooting and platform liability, not catastrophic risk from AI, so D.

record: Voted to advance H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, on utility costs from AI data centers.
Introduced H.R. 4873 to codify the executive order against 'woke' AI in the federal government (political bias in federal AI tools).
Sponsors the PROTECT Act (H.R. 7045) to repeal Section 230, which he links to harms from AI chatbots to children.
grade_reason: His 2026 remarks on AI are about children's safety, chatbot liability under Section 230 and data center electricity costs, all level D. No statement about catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus one extra on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. The superintelligence, extinction, pause and China searches returned nothing about him. The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar) cosponsors found in search results were Democrats; no source shows Patronis sponsored or co-signed it or any other House letter on AI risk, though a full cosponsor list on congress.gov was not opened.
